title: A king and a prince
html_source:
Throughout this chapter, Stephen’s theory that Shakespeare acted the part of Hamlet the father, not Hamlet the son, though agreeing with Eglinton that Shakespeare was, in a sense, both Hamlets, expresses a similar conundrum of how or how much Joyce “is” Stephen or Bloom (or both) in Ulysses.

It would be difficult to observe all the ways Joyce’s schema title of Scylla and Charybdis, i.e., trying to find a passage between two dangers, finds expression in the chapter, but this is as good a place as any to note one such expression. Hamlet the king or Hamlet the prince? Shakespeare the human being or Shakespeare’s work? Bloom or Stephen? On and on.
